The `HelpFormatter` class in the Apache Commons CLI library has a `printHelp` method that is used to print usage information for a set of options. The method takes in a `PrintWriter`, a width for the output, command line syntax, header, options, padding, and footer.

In the failing test case `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored`, the test sets up some `Options` with a long description and uses a `HelpFormatter` to print the help message. The expected output contains the long description split into multiple lines when the description is too long to fit on a single line.

The bug report describes an issue where the `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop and eventually crashes with an `OutOfMemoryError` when there is not enough space to display a word on a single line. This indicates a problem with the wrapping logic in the `HelpFormatter` class.

By looking at the code snippets for the `printHelp` method and the `getDescription` method of the `Option` class, we can infer that the issue may be related to how the long descriptions of options are handled and wrapped in the `HelpFormatter`.

To diagnose the root cause of the issue, we need to inspect the implementation of the `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class to see how it handles wrapping long descriptions of options. The problem likely lies in how the method calculates line breaks for long descriptions and how it handles cases where a word cannot fit on a single line within the specified width. We should check if there is any logic that causes the infinite loop when formatting long descriptions.

Inspecting and potentially modifying the `printHelp` method in the `HelpFormatter` class is likely the best location to fix the issue.

Next, I will suggest the best location to fix the bug.
The bug can likely be fixed by updating the `HelpFormatter.printHelp` method.

The best location to fix the bug is:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter,int,java.lang.String,java.lang.String,org.apache.commons.cli.Options,int,int,java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
